items.title: N-able says recent security breach led to major service outage
items.summary: N-able says attackers who breached one of its servers have caused a major outage affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services worldwide. On Tuesday, the company initially blamed the outage on what it described as a "combination of platform configuration and service dependencies" affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts services across the Americas, Asia-Pacific, and Europe. However, one day later, N-able disabled UI and API access and confirmed unauthorized access to a server in the Hosted Cloud environment. N-able also said the cyberattack didn't affect email flow or spam filtering and that it has yet to find evidence that the attackers gained access to customers' data and mailboxes. "Our earlier update said the disruption came from platform configuration and service dependencies and we believed we had remediated the issue. As we continued our investigation, we determined that the disruption was caused by a security incident affecting the Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud environment," the company said.

items.title: Dialing for Data: Inside the Com’s High-Profile Heists
items.summary: Unit 42 has tracked and responded to numerous waves of vishing attacks conducted by Com-affiliated threat actors in recent months. The attacks have led to data theft and extortion attempts. This activity has targeted data-rich industries, such as financial services, healthcare and legal services. Targeted organizations were primarily located in the U.S., UK and Australia. Attribution for this broad activity includes: - Named actors such as Bling Libra (aka ShinyHunters) - Activity clusters CL-CRI-1116 (aka Redact, formerly BlackFile), CL-CRI-1147 (aka Pink), CL-CRI-1182 (aka Falcon), CL-CRI-1192 (aka Helix) - The newly uncovered CL-CRI-1264 (aka Vortex) and CL-CRI-1274 (aka Cinder), which overlap with activity Google tracks as UNC6671 This article details: - Our observations of persistent Com-affiliated threat activity since August 2026 based on unique telemetry analysis and incident response engagements - The different named actors and activity clusters we track, including unique observations not previously disclosed - Insights on victimology - Review of attacker tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs) - Allusions to future activity as we head into 2027

items.title: pip bundles compromised eMudhra certificates via certifi
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv4.0: 9.3, CVEs: CVE-2026-133949, Summary: pip prior to v26.2.2 the certifi bundled with pip contains the compromised eMudhra certificates. Upgrading to a secure version of pip should be done either by first upgrading Python to a version that rejects the compromised intermediates (CVE-2026-115557) or use hash pinning with a known-secure version of pip. pip is not vulnerable when using a Python version that rejects the compromised certificates.

items.title: phpAfterShell and Critical PHP RCE Vulnerabilities: Everything You Need To Know
items.summary: On November 19, 2026, the PHP group published security updates addressing 17 vulnerabilities across all actively supported branches (PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5). Seven of these flaws are rated Critical (CVSS 9.2) and present direct pathways to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). Security teams are advised to identify and patch exposed PHP deployments, as earlier mitigation efforts implemented during October's response to "PHP2Shell" do not provide protection against all of these new exploit vectors. As of yet, no exploitation in the wild has been observed by Wiz or mentioned in public reporting.

items.title: West Virginia Legislature hit with cyber incident affecting IT systems
items.summary: West Virginia’s state legislature is responding to a cyberattack that has taken down its website and impacted IT systems. Ann Ali, deputy chief of staff for the House of Delegates, told Recorded Future News that the attack started on Thursday and has continued through Friday. “Upon discovery, the relevant teams immediately took steps to contain the incident and began an investigation with the help of outside cybersecurity specialists,” Ali said. “In connection with the investigation, access to certain Legislature IT systems has been temporarily disabled. However, based on what we know so far, the incident appears to be limited to the Legislature’s computer systems.” She added that no other state agencies or offices are impacted by the cyberattack. An investigation into the incident is ongoing but Ali did not respond to follow-up questions about whether it was a ransomware attack.

items.title: Signal restricts screenshots to block AI agents from reading messages
items.summary: Encrypted messaging service Signal said on Friday it would restrict screenshots to stop AI agents ​from reading private chats on phones, warning that the tech industry's push to embed AI in consumer devices was eroding its ability to guarantee ‌privacy. Signal, widely regarded by privacy advocates as a leader in secure messaging, called its new protections "incomplete" and urged operating system providers Apple (AAPL.O), opens new tab, Alphabet's (GOOGL.O), opens new tab Google and Microsoft (MSFT.O), opens new tab to give app developers more concrete ways to block the agents from accessing sensitive data. It also called on those companies to provide more information about how their agents function, so developers can assess what data the bots are accessing and adjust their systems accordingly. The ​move reflects growing tension between privacy-focused apps and the biggest tech companies, which are racing to roll out AI agents designed to see what is on a ​user's screen and take actions based on it. Signal identified as particularly worrisome the AI capabilities built directly into operating systems, like Apple's ⁠Siri AI and Google's Gemini Intelligence, because of how deeply they are integrated into people's devices.

items.title: KVM x86 vulnerability in Linux kernel
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 8.8, CVEs: CVE-2026-99312, Summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU context. Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role. Even though it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active, there's zero value in not handling SMM. At that point, the only scenario where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides most of the re-configuration in that case). Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while L2 is active. Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when CR0.PG must be '0').

items.title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
items.summary: Broadcom has released security updates to fix a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass vulnerability that Chinese-linked hackers have exploited in zero-day attacks since September 2026. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, affects the VMware Directory Service in vCenter Server, a management platform organizations use to manage VMware virtualized environments. According Broadcom, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a vulnerable vCenter Server to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Successful exploitation can allow attackers to obtain administrative access to vCenter, giving them control over the virtual machines managed by the server. "You are affected if you are running any version of VMware vCenter, SDDC Manager, or VMware Tools for Windows prior to the versions listed as "fixed" in the VMSA," Broadcom's security advisory reads. "This includes vCenter and SDDC Manager deployed standalone and as part of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSphere Foundation, VMware Telco Cloud Platform, and VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure, as well as VMware Tools installed in Windows virtual machines." The company considers the vCenter vulnerability as an emergency update, urging organizations to install the patches as soon as possible. Broadcom says there are no official workarounds for the vulnerabilities, although network restrictions and firewall controls can help reduce exposure. Furthermore, the vulnerability affects vCenter regardless of whether Enhanced Linked Mode is enabled. While Broadcom has not confirmed that the flaw was exploited, researchers at Google's Mandiant have documented attacks exploiting CVE-2026-123890.

items.title: Second Norwegian Energy Company Breached in 2 Days
items.summary: Two Norwegian energy companies announced that they'd been breached on two consecutive days this week. On the evening of Nov. 17, Equinor — one of the world's most economically and geopolitically significant oil and gas companies — announced that it had suffered a cyberattack. Hardly a day later, another billion-dollar Norwegian energy company called Skagerak Energi admitted to the same. The two companies' breach disclosures read remarkably similarly, though there is no evidence yet that the two attacks are connected. Equinor did not respond to a request for comment on this story. Skagerak Energi declined to comment on specifics of the company's incident. Equinor first publicly reported its cyberattack on the evening of Nov. 17, Central European Time (CET). Its initial investigation suggested that no data had been stolen, and that operations and production would remain uninterrupted. The issue seemed to be limited to internal IT systems. For instance, one employee told Reuters that the company's email system was down.

items.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
items.summary: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register. “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.”

items.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
items.summary: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP, Java, and PostgreSQL, VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890, a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. [...] Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312, a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5.
